items.value: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct; statement 3 is wrong because the notified PVTG count is 75, not 95
items.reasoning: PVTGs are officially recorded as living in 18 States and the Union Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands, so statement 1 holds. The four criteria for PVTG identification are a pre-agricultural level of technology, a low level of literacy, economic backwardness and a stagnant or declining population, so statement 2 holds. The number notified is 75, not 95, so statement 3 fails. Irular (Tamil Nadu and Kerala) and Konda Reddi (Andhra Pradesh) are both on the PVTG list, so statement 4 holds. Only option C carries exactly 1, 2 and 4, and it is also the only option that omits the false statement 3.

items.value: The Supreme Court's power under Article 142 to do complete justice is not fettered by ordinary statutes made by Parliament
items.reasoning: Article 142 empowers the Supreme Court to pass any decree or order necessary for doing complete justice in a cause before it. The proposition quoted in the stem is the settled position that this constitutional power cannot be cut down by restrictions written into ordinary legislation, which is exactly what option B states. Option A concerns Article 329 and the Election Commission, option C concerns Article 360 and the aid-and-advice rule, and option D concerns the legislative-list scheme under Articles 246 and 254 — none of them turns on Article 142.

items.value: Both statements are correct: the Governor addresses the House at the start of the first session of each year, and a State legislature falls back on Lok Sabha practice where its own rules are silent
items.reasoning: Article 176 requires the Governor to address the Legislative Assembly at the commencement of the first session after each general election and at the commencement of the first session of each year, so statement 1 is correct. The rules of procedure of State legislatures carry a residuary provision under which matters not covered by their own rules are regulated in accordance with the practice and procedure of the Lok Sabha, so statement 2 is correct as a description of actual practice. Runner-up is A (1 only), which would win if the item is read as demanding a binding legal rule rather than a settled convention, since no constitutional provision compels a State House to follow Lok Sabha rules.

items.value: Only statements 2 and 4 are correct — UNCAC is the first legally binding global anti-corruption instrument and UNODC services both conventions; the migrant-smuggling protocol and the asset-recovery chapter are attributed to the wrong treaties
items.reasoning: The Protocol against the Smuggling of Migrants by Land, Sea and Air is one of the three protocols to the UN Convention against Transnational Organized Crime (the Palermo Convention), not to UNCAC, so statement 1 is false. UNCAC (2003) is indeed the first legally binding global anti-corruption instrument, so statement 2 is true. The dedicated chapter on asset recovery and the return of assets to their rightful owners is the celebrated feature of UNCAC, not of UNTOC, so statement 3 is false — the item has deliberately swapped the two treaties' signature features. UNODC is the custodian and guardian of both conventions, so statement 4 is true. Only option C contains exactly 2 and 4.

items.value: Only statements 2 and 3 are correct — bamboo is a minor forest produce that forest dwellers may own under the FRA, but the Indian Forest Act amendment de-classified bamboo only on non-forest land
items.reasoning: The 2017 amendment to the Indian Forest Act, 1927 removed bamboo from the definition of 'tree' only where it grows on non-forest land; bamboo grown inside forest areas continues to be treated as a tree and cannot be freely felled, so statement 1 is false. Section 2(i) of the Forest Rights Act, 2006 expressly includes bamboo within 'minor forest produce', so statement 2 is true. Section 3(1)(c) of the same Act confers on forest dwellers the right of ownership, access to collect, use and dispose of minor forest produce, so statement 3 is true. Of the two options that exclude the false statement 1, only B also includes the true statement 2.

items.value: Article 21 — the right to marry a person of one's choice is read into the right to life and personal liberty
items.reasoning: The Supreme Court has held in Lata Singh, Shakti Vahini and Shafin Jahan (the Hadiya case) that the choice of a life partner is intrinsic to the dignity and personal liberty guaranteed by Article 21, and that neither the State nor family may interfere with an adult's marital choice. Article 19 covers the six freedoms of speech, assembly, association, movement, residence and profession; Article 25 covers freedom of religion; Article 29 protects the cultural and educational interests of minorities — none of these is the source of the right in question.

items.value: Only statement 3 is correct — plant varieties cannot be patented in India; biological processes for producing seeds are also excluded, and the IPAB did exist
items.reasoning: Section 3(j) of the Patents Act, 1970 excludes from patentability plants and animals in whole or any part thereof, including seeds and varieties, and essentially biological processes for their production or propagation, so statement 1 is false and statement 3 is true. Plant varieties are protected instead under the sui generis Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Act, 2001. The Intellectual Property Appellate Board was constituted in 2003 and was functioning at the time of this paper (it was abolished only in 2021), so statement 2 is false. Only option C names statement 3 alone.

items.value: Both are correct — the Act empowers the Centre both to lay down emission and discharge standards and to prescribe requirements and procedure for public participation in environmental protection
items.reasoning: Section 3(2)(iv) of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 expressly empowers the Central Government to lay down standards for emission or discharge of environmental pollutants from various sources, so statement 2 is plainly correct. Statement 1 rests on the wide enabling power in Section 3(1) read with the rule-making power in Section 25: the Environment (Protection) Rules and the EIA Notification issued under this Act are precisely where the requirement of public consultation and the manner of conducting a public hearing are prescribed, and Section 19 lets any citizen prosecute after 60 days' notice. Runner-up is B (2 only), which would win on a strict reading that the bare text of the Act nowhere uses the words 'public participation' and that the procedure appears only in subordinate legislation.

items.value: The Rules do lay down detailed, specific criteria for siting landfills and waste-processing facilities
items.reasoning: Schedule I of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016 prescribes precise siting criteria — minimum distances from rivers, ponds, highways, habitations, and a 20 km separation from airports and airbases, along with buffer-zone and no-development requirements — so option C is correct. Option A is wrong because the Rules require segregation into three streams (biodegradable, non-biodegradable or dry, and domestic hazardous waste), not five. Option B is wrong because the word 'only' excludes the many other areas the 2016 Rules brought in for the first time, including census towns, notified areas, railway and airport premises, ports, defence establishments, SEZs and places of pilgrimage. Option D is wrong because no such inter-district movement bar exists.

items.value: Both are correct — fixed-term employment makes it easier for firms to shed workers, and no notice of termination is required for a temporary workman
items.reasoning: The Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Central (Amendment) Rules, 2018 extended fixed-term employment to all sectors; a fixed-term contract simply lapses on expiry, which is not treated as retrenchment, so the employer escapes the notice, compensation and prior-permission requirements of the Industrial Disputes Act — statement 1 is therefore correct as an effect of the rules. The Model Standing Orders provide that no notice of termination is necessary in the case of a temporary workman, whether monthly rated, weekly rated or piece rated, so statement 2 is correct. Runner-up is B (2 only), which would win if statement 1 is rejected as an editorial inference about consequences rather than a provision of the Rules themselves.

items.value: The Lead Bank Scheme
items.reasoning: The Service Area Approach was introduced by the Reserve Bank of India in 1989 as part of the Lead Bank Scheme, assigning each rural and semi-urban bank branch a specific cluster of villages for planned credit deployment and orderly area development. It is a banking-sector credit-planning device, unconnected with the Integrated Rural Development Programme's asset-subsidy design, with MGNREGS's employment guarantee, or with the National Skill Development Mission.

items.value: Only statements 1 and 3 are correct — sand is a minor mineral and States can frame anti-illegal-mining rules, but rule-making for minor minerals rests with the States, not the Centre
items.reasoning: Section 3(e) of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957 defines 'minor minerals' to include ordinary sand, so statement 1 is true. Section 15 vests in the State Governments the power to make rules for regulating the grant of quarry leases, mining leases and other mineral concessions in respect of minor minerals, so statement 2 is false — it reverses the actual allocation. Section 23C empowers State Governments to frame rules to prevent illegal mining, transportation and storage of minerals, so statement 3 is true. Of the two options excluding the false statement 2, only A also carries the true statement 1.

items.value: Neither statement is correct — most of India's external debt is non-government, and it is denominated in several currencies besides the US dollar
items.reasoning: Sovereign or government external debt is only about a fifth of India's total external debt; the bulk is non-government commercial borrowings, NRI deposits and short-term trade credit, so statement 1 is false. India's external debt is denominated in a basket of currencies — the US dollar is the largest share at roughly half, but the Indian rupee, SDR, Japanese yen and euro all account for meaningful portions — so the absolute claim in statement 2 is false. With both wrong, the answer is D.

items.value: Deposits, which are a liability of the bank and not an asset
items.reasoning: A commercial bank's balance sheet places deposits on the liabilities side, because they are money the bank owes to its customers and must repay on demand or at maturity. Advances (loans made), investments (securities held) and money at call and short notice (very short-term lending in the money market) are all claims the bank holds against others, so all three are assets. The odd one out is therefore deposits.

items.value: Only 1 and 3 — IT export earnings and remittances both bring in foreign exchange and cushion the currency; higher government expenditure does not
items.reasoning: A currency crisis becomes less likely when a country has steady, non-debt-creating inflows of foreign exchange to cover its external obligations. India's software and IT services exports and inward remittances from Indians abroad are exactly such inflows, and both are the classic offsets to India's merchandise trade deficit, so statements 1 and 3 are contributors. Increasing government expenditure widens the fiscal deficit and, through higher demand for imports, tends to worsen the current account and weaken the currency, so statement 2 works in the opposite direction.

items.value: The Sarkaria Commission
items.reasoning: The Sarkaria Commission on Centre-State Relations laid down four qualifications for a Governor in almost these words: he should be an eminent person in some walk of life, a person from outside the State, a detached figure not too intimately connected with the local politics of the State, and a person who has not taken too great a part in politics generally and particularly in the recent past. The stem reproduces this formulation, so the attribution is to Sarkaria rather than to the First Administrative Reforms Commission, the Rajamannar Committee (a Tamil Nadu State committee focused on greater State autonomy) or the NCRWC.

items.value: Participatory Notes
items.reasoning: Participatory Notes, or P-Notes, are offshore derivative instruments issued by SEBI-registered foreign portfolio investors against underlying Indian securities, allowing overseas investors to take exposure to Indian stocks without themselves registering with SEBI. A Certificate of Deposit is a negotiable money-market instrument issued by banks, Commercial Paper is an unsecured short-term instrument issued by corporates, and a Promissory Note is a general debt instrument — none of them is an offshore route into the Indian equity market.

items.value: Only statement 1 is correct — CAMPA exists at both national and State levels, but the Act does not make people's participation mandatory
items.reasoning: The Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016 provides for a National Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority and a State authority in every State and Union Territory, so statement 1 is correct. The Act and its Rules contain no mandatory requirement of people's participation, and the absence of any gram sabha consent or community-participation obligation — despite the Forest Rights Act — has been one of the principal criticisms of the legislation, so statement 2 is false.

items.value: Only 1 and 2 — ad hoc parliamentary committees and the department-related standing committees
items.reasoning: Independent sectoral regulators such as TRAI, IRDAI and the electricity regulatory commissions are accountable to Parliament, which scrutinises them through the department-related standing committees attached to the relevant ministries and, where needed, through ad hoc committees constituted for a specific inquiry. The Finance Commission is a constitutional body confined to recommending the distribution of tax revenues between the Union and the States, and NITI Aayog is a policy think tank with no review mandate over regulators; the Financial Sector Legislative Reforms Commission was a one-time body that examined only financial-sector laws, not telecom or electricity. Every option other than A includes at least one of these three.

items.value: Only statements 1 and 2 are correct — the Second Plan pushed basic and capital goods and the Fourth Plan targeted concentration of economic power; the Fifth Plan claim about the financial sector is wrong
items.reasoning: The Second Five-Year Plan, built on the Mahalanobis model, made a deliberate push towards heavy, basic and capital goods industries and towards import substitution in those goods, so statement 1 is correct. The Fourth Plan (1969-74) set out growth with stability and progressive self-reliance and explicitly sought to check the concentration of wealth and economic power — the MRTP Act of 1969 belongs to this period — so statement 2 is correct. The Fifth Plan (1974-79) was framed around removal of poverty and attainment of self-reliance, not around bringing the financial sector into the Plan for the first time, so statement 3 is false. Runner-up is D, which would win if statement 3 is accepted; a reviewer should check the Fifth Plan's stated objectives against that claim.

items.value: Only statement 1 is correct — AIIB's membership exceeds 80, but China and not India is the largest shareholder, and AIIB has many non-regional members
items.reasoning: AIIB grew from 57 founding members in 2016 to well over 80 approved members by 2019, so statement 1 is correct. China is by far the largest shareholder with roughly a quarter to a third of the voting power; India is the second largest, so statement 2 is false. AIIB deliberately admits non-regional members, and the United Kingdom, Germany, France, Canada and others from outside Asia are members, so statement 3 is false. Since statements 2 and 3 are both false, every option except A is eliminated regardless of how strictly statement 1 is read.

items.value: To speed up resolution of stressed assets of Rs 50 crore or more held under consortium or multiple-banking arrangements
items.reasoning: The Inter-Creditor Agreement of 2018 flowed from the Sunil Mehta Committee's Project Sashakt proposals. It binds the lenders in a consortium to a common framework in which a resolution plan approved by lenders holding a specified majority of the outstanding exposure becomes binding on all, so that a single dissenting bank can no longer stall resolution of a large stressed account. It has nothing to do with the fiscal or current account deficit, with financing government infrastructure projects, or with acting as a regulator over loan applications.

items.value: The Banks Board Bureau
items.reasoning: The Banks Board Bureau, set up in 2016 on the recommendation of the P. J. Nayak Committee, is the body that recommends candidates for appointment as whole-time directors and non-executive chairmen of public sector banks and financial institutions, and advises on their governance. The Reserve Bank of India is the banking regulator but does not select PSB chairmen, the Finance Ministry acts on the Bureau's recommendations rather than making the selection itself, and the management of a bank cannot appoint its own chairman.

items.value: Only statements 2 and 3 are correct — PNGRB promotes competitive gas markets and appeals from it lie to the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity, but it is not India's first regulator
items.reasoning: PNGRB was constituted under the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board Act, 2006 and began functioning in 2007; SEBI (1992), TRAI (1997) and the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (1998) all predate it, so statement 1 is false. The Act's preamble and Section 11 charge the Board with protecting consumer interests and ensuring competitive markets for petroleum, petroleum products and natural gas, so statement 2 is true. Section 33 of the Act makes the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity the appellate authority against PNGRB's orders, so statement 3 is true. Only option B excludes the false statement 1 while keeping both true ones.

items.value: Neither statement states a real difference — LTE is marketed as 4G, not 3G, and VoLTE is not a voice-only technology
items.reasoning: LTE is universally marketed as 4G and VoLTE as an enhancement over 4G, not as 3G and advanced 3G, so statement 1 is false. LTE is indeed an all-IP, packet-switched data-bearing technology, but VoLTE is not voice-only: it carries voice as packets over that same LTE data network and lets voice and high-speed data run simultaneously on the same connection, which is precisely its advantage over circuit-switched fallback. Since the second half of statement 2 is wrong, the statement as a whole fails, and neither point survives.
